translation_notes: prefixes: QUDT->qudt, OA->oa, CSVW->csvw, RDF->rdf, XSD->xsd

self.g is a mutated-in-place function parameter, never reassigned: one `@graph g` at the top of the function covers the whole body, so every g.add(...) becomes a bare +{ } (no per-triple (g) suffix needed).

oa:value's Literal(cell, datatype=format) has a datatype decided at run time from the CSVW column's format; `{cell}^^{format}` (interpolation with a glued, itself-interpolated datatype) reproduces it exactly -- a genuine 'typed literal' use, safe here because cell is already a str (see instructions Sec.2bis on the Literal(x, datatype=) pitfall).

preserved two pre-existing bugs verbatim rather than fixing them: row_uri = "table-{TABLE}-gid-{GID}".format(table) (positional arg into named placeholders, only reachable when about_url is falsy -- the fixture keeps about_url truthy for every table to avoid an unrelated crash on both sides), and the anyURI branch's `else: value_node = URIRef(cell)`, which len(cell.split(' ')) >= 1 makes unreachable for any string including "".

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `@prefix` for `rdf:`, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.

repair.driver: deuxième appel (_make_self_typed) : table avec csvw:skipRows=2 et headerRowCount=1 (le csvw:url .../row=N dépend des deux termes de row_num), colonnes xsd:boolean ("True", "1", ""), xsd:date, xsd:dateTime (avec et sans fuseau) et xsd:int ("007"), cellules toujours str comme dans le dépôt (parse_csv_from_url_to_list applique str()), de sorte que le datatype calculé de oa:value n'est plus toujours xsd:string ; docstring mise à jour.
repair.remaining: Jugements non traités (drapeau wrong-construction) : l'IRI csvw:url reste en {URIRef("{}/row={}".format(...))} au lieu de f<{self.csv_url}/row={row_num}> (le triage l'a vérifié équivalent).

credit_correction.what: unused prefix declarations dropped from translated.ldpy

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the if/else on about_url becomes `or`; `columns` keeps only the values; the two-step French decimal rewrite is one expression; `value_node = BNode()` is hoisted out of the three branches; the unreachable `else: value_node = URIRef(cell)` of the anyURI branch (len(split) >= 1 is always true) and its comment go, as do `uris`; runs of g.add become `g += [...]`; the aboutUrl/name branches compute a `predicate` and share one g.add; row_num fits one line and the url uses an f-string.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: each `g += [...]` becomes one `+{ }` with `;`; Literal(cell) is a bare {cell}, Literal(cell, datatype=format) is `{cell}^^{format}`; URIRef(x) becomes f<{x}> (no @base).
Exceptions to the symmetry, island only: `row_node` and `body_node` disappear, written as Turtle anonymous blank nodes `[ ... ]` (each is used in a single island); Python needs the BNode() variable.

Not in the closed vocabulary: the Turtle blank-node property list `[ ... ]` inside +{ } (reported, not labelled). Collection(g, value_node, ...) is kept on both sides: the list head is value_node itself, which a Turtle `( )` cannot name.
header_optimization_notes: Python: nothing unused, optimized_header.py is a copy of optimized.py.
LD Python: Namespace and the rdflib.namespace import (CSVW, RDF, XSD) go, replaced by the four @prefix lines, all used.
